What you can put in a story

A place on a date

Borders as they stood on a given day, from 123,000 BC to today, on the same map as the present.

Data layers

165 data layers — from earthquakes and volcanoes to climate and infrastructure — each with its source named.

Interactive or still

By default readers can pan and zoom. One switch makes the frame a still picture of exactly your view.

How to embed, in five steps

  1. Open the map

    Open IntMap and move to the place you are reporting on.

  2. Set the date and the layers

    Move the clock to the date you need and switch on the layers that tell the story.

  3. Open Share, then Embed

    The Share button turns the view into a link; its Embed tab turns the same link into an iframe.

  4. Choose a size

    480×320, 640×400 or 960×600, or full width. Choose whether readers may pan and zoom.

  5. Paste it into your page

    Paste the code into your CMS where it accepts HTML. The frame loads lazily and shows no sign-in, no pop-up and no button of the app.

Questions newsrooms ask

Do we have to pay?

No fee is charged for embedding the public map. If your organisation is commercial and you want to be sure your use does not fall under the software licence's commercial clause, ask us first and we will answer in writing.

Will the embed keep showing the same thing?

The embed carries the whole view — place, date, layers — in its address. A historical date shows the same borders. A live layer (earthquakes, for example) shows the data as it stands when a reader opens it; for a fixed record of a moment, use a screenshot with the credits. IntMap offers no service-level guarantee.

Can we use a screenshot in print?

Keep the credit line of the map with the picture and check the licence of each layer you show on the data sources page; some sources set conditions of their own. Ask us if a source is unclear.

Do readers get tracked?

IntMap shows no advertising and uses no third-party analytics. The privacy policy lists every service the map contacts and what it sends.

Can you make a map for a specific story?

Write to us with what you need. We will tell you honestly whether IntMap can show it, and how.

What it costs

IntMap is free to use and is paid for by donations. There is no paid plan today. A paid plan for heavier use of the AI features may come later; what it would include and cost has not been decided, and anything free today stays free.

Licences

Every dataset keeps its own licence and credit; the data sources page lists them. The map's credit line names the sources of what is drawn and stays visible in an embed. IntMap's own software is free for personal, educational and non-profit research use; commercial use of the software needs a separate licence (LICENSE §3). If you are unsure which applies to you, ask before you publish.
